ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, input A branches on the left; one path enters the upper single-input gate marked “1”, and the output terminal of this gate has a small inversion circle; the other path goes downward and, together with input B, enters the lower AND gate marked “&”, and the output terminal of this AND gate also has a small inversion circle. The two intermediate outputs then enter the OR gate on the right marked “≥1”, and the right output terminal also has a small inversion circle, with output Y. Then reason: The output of the upper branch is the inversion of A, namely overline(A). The lower branch is first AB, and then after inversion at the output terminal it obtains overline(AB). The “≥1” on the right represents an OR operation, and the inversion at the output terminal represents taking the inverse of the OR of the two inputs, so Y = overline(overline(A) + overline(AB)). By De Morgan's law, Y = A · AB.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: A splits into an upper single-input gate and a lower AND gate; B joins only the lower AND gate; both intermediate outputs are inverted, and then they enter a final OR gate with an inverted output Y. Translate each stage into Boolean algebra: upper branch gives \(\overline A\), lower branch gives \(\overline{AB}\), final stage gives \(Y=\overline{\overline A+\overline{AB}}\). Use De Morgan’s law to obtain \(Y=A\cdot AB\).
